title: Summer's Lease
subtitle: They turn their heads as the first leaf flutters to the ground.

items.text: Inn, Zhu County
Reed sits quietly by the bed.
No sign of her spider friend. No glow from the brooch on her chest.
She has walked every street in the city but never found an answer. It was all in vain.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Nope, wind's still giving me nothing.
A few dry leaves break off from her head, drifting toward her pillow.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Maybe I should leave so I can contact Ms. Verity and then decide if I want to head back.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: No. It's all too suspicious. She'd tell me to abort, for sure.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: *sigh* Basically, I should give up and just go back to headquarters. I could pick another topic to work on if I still have time.
How much time do you have left?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Time. Hah. Like I've ever had that.
The budding writer lets out a short laugh at her own expense as she picks up a fallen leaf from the bed and smooths it flat.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Winter's coming.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'll have withered by then. Even if another reed'll sprout from my body next year, "I" will be gone for good.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: The inevitable end of every ephemeral plant.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Mayfly ... She was one of us. I wonder what happened to her. Did she find a way to keep on living?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hrmph.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I can't. I just can't accept that I'll die without finishing my article, especially when I'm, like, a single step away from finding a way to stay me.
She places the blade of grass between the pages of her notebook.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: That's that. I just need to keep going. Besides, these knots are an anomaly that needs to be fixed anyway; why shouldn't I be the one to do it?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Alright, forget about whatever this OneWithFlow's trying. I'll just do my thing.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I-I have to finish this article.
Reed closes her notebook and steps out the door.
Once more, the wind seems to pull at her, nearly tearing her mind straight out of her body. The gust leaves behind an uneasy feeling in her stomach.
She bears the feeling and waits for the fall she knows is coming.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Is this another of Mayfly's memories?
A brief sadness rises in her, then a faintly familiar voice cuts it off.
Chief?
May I enter?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Please.
City Defense Office, Ancient Zhu County
After settling the disturbance, Dù Liù makes his way to the town's constabulary office and knocks at the door of his chief.
At the desk, Chéng Héguāng bends over a mess of documents.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Sir, the Daoist has lifted the spell. Several people in the crowd were injured by that yellow dog; we've sent them to get treatment.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Order has been restored at the gate. Inspections are ongoing.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: The Daoist and her mule are locked up. She's ready for interrogation. Yáng Wǔ is watching her.
The chief nods, barely looking up from his files.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Good. Return to your position. I will go to see her immediately.
Dù Liù looks down over the papers, letting out an unintended grumble as he realizes their meaning.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Ah. Forgive me, Chief, but isn't that someone else's job? I fail to see why we should bother investigating these animal carcasses. I know the Stilted Parade is about to begin, but—

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: You understand the importance of this for the people, do you not? We must leave no stone unturned.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Yes, but even so, it seems a waste of our men's time to look into a few dead animals?

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: There's no proof that they were killed by Yao. Perhaps it was some beasts in the mountain that chased them here.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: And even if it was a Yao, there's no need to take it so seriously. It's best to leave them to their own affairs.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: "Their own affairs"?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: All residents of the Ming Empire, be they human or Yao, are bound under the same law, and it is our duty to uphold it.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: You know as well as I do that something is afoot here. Those carcasses are involved in all this. I can feel it.
He points at the file in his hand.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: This report just reached me. Another carcass was found in Chunhua Alley this morning.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Like the others, it was intact, yet pale and dry. There were also sightings of the same mysterious parade near the scene.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: They were spreading rumors about the Method of Longevity. They have already amassed a small following.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: And do not forget Commander Lì's orders: we must make sure the fair is without blemish. This risk is too large to ignore.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: But, Chief Chéng, the men have been working for weeks without rest. They're exhausted. If we give them more work—
Dù Liù doesn't have time to finish his complaint before another knock interrupts him.

items.speaker: Constable I
items.text: Chief, Yáng Wǔ is expecting you.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Understood. I'll be there shortly.
His subordinate decides to bite back his words.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: I must go. Excuse me, Chief.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Hold on! Hmm.
Dù Liù waits, already expecting his next words.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I, hmm, I know that everyone has been working hard of late, and I am sincerely grateful for their efforts.
He stumbles to find the right words.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: So, let them know, once the fair is over, I will take them to the finest restaurant in town.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: My treat.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Much appreciated. But I'm certain even a chief's salary couldn't cover such a meal.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: I'll have their bellies filled before we go. We wouldn't want to embarrass you, huh?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: No need. The chef there is a friend. They won't charge me much if I bring the ingredients myself. Bass is in season.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Oh, you're bringing bass? I'll tell the men to skip lunch then.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Still the record holder of the Fishing Competition, aren't you? Who else but Chéng could pull up a bass half his size?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Please, Dù Liù, it's just a way to make some extra wen. Right, enough talk. Back to work.

items.speaker: Du Liu
items.text: Yes, Chief Chéng! I'll take my leave then.
He leaves, and the young officer returns to his files.
The mist rises again, covering the scene before her and then dissolving away.
The darkness is familiar now. She waits for the inn's open window to return to her sight.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: That wasn't Mayfly's memory. How many people are involved in this story? Are they somehow connected to each other?
Perhaps this will make things clearer.
Wind screams past her, pulling her again toward some distant, unknown place.
Her thoughts sink first, spreading like roots digging into the earth. Then, a nursery rhyme lifts them up.
